rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All are gathered only to God: responders join the believers, while those who turn away are counted among unbelievers even if they refuse only one ruling, because religion is indivisible.
rows.anchor: فيحشر المستجيبين في زمرة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition does not restrict the command to particular calls; it reminds believers to follow every call of the infallible Messenger, who has called them to every good.
rows.anchor: وقدم علم أن ) إذا ( ليست قيدا وإنما هي تنبيه على وجوب اتباعه في كل ما يدعو إليه لعصمته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali calls the general prophetic protection preservation under the prior revealed law; protection from faults in conveyance, degrading acts, and major sins is agreed, while minor sins are disputed and some allow a prohibited act as an unfinished preliminary.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي في أواخر كتاب له في أصوال الفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the Prophet Muhammad is elevated above the debate about whether prophets may commit minor sins.
rows.anchor: فإن المتحقق من أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما هو علو عن هذا المحل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali’s special protection for Muhammad makes his acts the source and indicator of rulings at each moment; they are not judged by prior law or his understanding of earlier practice.
rows.anchor: المعنى الثاني من العصمة رفع الحكم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بما حفظه الحافظ من ماضي ظاهر شرعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr and Ibn Umar exemplified close imitation, following even the Prophet’s way of turning his mount, yellow dye, and sandals.
rows.anchor: فمن كان يسبق إليه من أكبار الصحابة نحو من هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When someone continued his prayer after being called, the Prophet corrected his assumption by citing this command to answer God and the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أي بقوله : ألم تسمع الله يقول { استجيبوا لله وللرسول }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet repeatedly ordered a man to descend and harvest; after the man cited daylight, he insisted a third or fourth time, illustrating the authority of his call.
rows.anchor: فقال له في الثالثة أو الرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet’s act establishes its ruling, following him without first specifying the ruling is valid; an ambiguous intention to imitate may exceed acting on a ruling already clarified.
rows.anchor: فإذا وضح أن فعله مبدأ الحكم ومعلم الإنباء لزم صحة التأسي به على مطلق التأسي مع إبهام رتبة الحكم

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: While in Yemen, Ali set out for Mecca in the same state of consecration as the Prophet, an example of following his practice.
rows.anchor: أحرم علي رضي الله عنه وهو باليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparently differing prophetic rulings reflect hearers’ incomplete grasp of his knowledge, not contradiction: valid jihad expiates sins before God, while a debt still requires satisfying its claimant.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر له ما قال جبرائيل عليه السلام من استثناء الدين الدين مما أنزل على حكم أمر الله في محكم شرعته وسنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who followed the Prophet’s initial directive about pollination obtained fruit for three years, then returned without pollination to an even better yield; the example illustrates acting on his instruction.
rows.anchor: فقد عمل بأول فتياه غير واحد ممن لم يتسرب في نفاد حكمه وصحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic act that conveys an obligation saves from punishment; one that teaches nearness to God leads to His love. If its status is unclear, imitate while learning the intent.
rows.anchor: فكل فعل فعله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن كان بياتا لواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to follow the Messenger is linked to the promise that following him brings God’s love, as stated in 3:31; where an act’s status is unclear, imitate him and learn its intent.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يتضح له مجمل منهما تأسى بها على إبهام بغنيه علمه وتعلموا به نيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act specific to the Prophet must be explicitly identified as exclusive by God or the Prophet, as in the exception stated in 33:50.
rows.anchor: وما كان مختصا به فلا بد من إظهار أمر اختصاصه بخطاب من الله سبحانه أو منه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet received one fifth of the fifth during his life for Muslim interests, then his successor used it as he had; the Prophet’s kin are Hashim and Muttalib, barred from zakat, alongside orphans, the poor, and travelers.
rows.anchor: اي يصرف إليه خمس هذا الخمس ما دام حيا ليصرفه في مصالح المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not deprive the believers of spoils: He granted victory, permitted the spoils, left them four fifths, and returned the remaining fifth among them; they should give thanks, not dispute as entitled claimants.
rows.anchor: فالحاصل انه سبحانه لم يرزأكم من المغنم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God and what He sent to His servant includes the Qur’an, troops, and tranquility sent swiftly to relieve the believers; Badr is the Day of Criterion that gave them honor and decisive agency.
rows.anchor: أي إنزالا واحدا سريعا لأحل التفريج عنكم من القرآن والجنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the day the two groups met adds that the encounter was not planned by either side but arranged by God; merely saying ‘the day of Badr’ would omit this lesson.
rows.anchor: أي عن غير قصد من الفرقين بل بمخص تدبير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer bank was closer to Medina; the farther bank lay farther from it, nearer the sea.
rows.anchor: بالعدوة الدنيا } اي القربى إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read al-ʿudwa with kasra; the other readers read it with damma.
rows.anchor: بالكسر في قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected form would turn the waw into a ya, and that form occurs, but the form with waw is more common, as with istawsaba versus the rarer istasaba.
rows.anchor: والقياس قلب واوه ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿudwa is a bank or edge of a valley; its root-field turns on agitation and related ideas of adjacency, stillness, turning, return, and racing, suggesting raised ground beside a stream.
rows.anchor: فكأنها الموضع الذي علا عن محل فكان السيل موضعا للعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan was the trading party the Muslims had hoped to intercept, led by Abu Sufyan; it lay below both armies toward the sea, about three miles away according to al-Baghawi.
rows.anchor: أي العير الذي فيه المتجر الذي خرجتم لاقتطاعه ورئيس جماعته أبو سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan’s location and the Quraysh army’s confident position show how much stronger the enemy appeared and how weak the Muslims were, making their victory a divine act.
rows.anchor: وإلى مثل هذه المعاني أشار تصوير مكانهم ومكان الركب إيماء إلى ما كان فيه العدو من قوة الشوكة وتكامل العدة وتمهد أسباب الغلبة وضعف حال المسلمين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Salama ibn Salama ibn Waqsh disparaged the defeated Quraysh as bald old women, the Prophet replied that they were leaders whose sight would inspire fear and whose orders Salama would obey.
rows.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لسلمة بن سلامة بن وقش رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against al-Baydawi, following al-Kashshaf, the near bank was not uniquely waterless and sinking sand: Muslims reached the water first, and rain compacted their ground while impeding the enemy.
rows.anchor: وما في البيضاوي تبعا للكشاف من أن العدوة الدنيا كانت تسوخ فيها الأقدام ولا ماء بها تقدم زده أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A planned meeting would likely have failed because the camps were far apart and could not coordinate their pace, and because the Muslims feared the enemy; God could also have made Quraysh avoid the meeting, as at Badr al-Mawʿid.
rows.anchor: أحدهما بعد المسافة التي كنتم بها منها وتعذر توقيت سير كل فريق بسير صاحبه

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl said that if the conflict were against people, Quraysh were strong enough, but if Muhammad’s claim that they fought God were true, nobody could withstand God; he also admitted to al-Akhnas that Muhammad never lied.
rows.anchor: قول أبي جهل الذي كان السبب الأعظم في اللقاء

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl told al-Akhnas ibn Shariq that Muhammad was truthful and had never lied, even as God hardened the enemy’s hearts to bring about the encounter.
rows.anchor: وقوله أيضا في هذه الغزوة للأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God arranged the unplanned meeting: need drew the Muslims toward the caravan, they were promised one of two parties, Quraysh were compelled to defend it, and its escape left them arriving at Badr in pride and display.
rows.anchor: فأطمعكم في العير أولا

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl vowed not to return until Quraysh sacrificed camels, drank wine, and entertained themselves at Badr so that the Arabs would fear them thereafter; this displays their pride before defeat.
rows.anchor: لا نرجع حتى نرد بدرا فننحر بها الجزور ونشرب الخمور وتعزف علينا القيان ونطعم من حضرنا من العرب فلا يزالون يهابوننا مدى الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s predetermined decree exalted His religion by honoring the Muslims and humiliating Quraysh, bringing about their killing and capture as destined.
rows.anchor: أي مقدرا في الأزل من لقائهم وما وقع فيه

words: لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَيَّ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary outcome let each side perish or live on clear evidence: Badr proved the Messenger’s promises true and his opponents’ confident claims false despite appearances favoring them.
rows.anchor: لما بان من صدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الوقعة في كل ما وعد به وكذب الكفار في كل ما كانوا يقولونه قاطعين به مع أن ظاهر الحال يقضي لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir, and Abu Bakr from Asim pronounce both yāʾs distinctly, signaling fullest life through Islam; the remaining readers assimilate them, signaling lesser life.
rows.anchor: قراءة نافع والبزي عن ابن كثير وأبي بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who later say that their religion has deluded them reveal who was truly deceived; God hears their statements and knows their concealed thoughts, so they should fear Him and abandon their dispute.
rows.anchor: فيحنئذ تبين المغرور وكشفت عجائب المقدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what they say and knows what they conceal; this should humble them and turn them from disputing out of fear.
rows.anchor: أي لما كنتم تقولونه وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed the Prophet the enemy as few in a dream, and his report reassured and encouraged the Companions; the vision and ensuing course were God’s work, not their choice.
rows.anchor: فحدث اصحاب رضي الله عنه بذلك فاطمأنت قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the Prophet seen the enemy as numerous, the Companions would have lost courage, disputed, and weakened; God spared them this because He knows their hearts before thoughts arise.
rows.anchor: { لفشلتم } أي جبنتم { ولتنازعتم } أي اختلفتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protected the Muslims from the collapse that a frightening vision would have caused because He knows the hearts’ courage and fear before either enters conscious thought.
rows.anchor: وغيرهما قبل خطورها في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the encounter God made the enemy look few in Muslim eyes, though they were not few in reality; this confirmed the dream and emboldened the Muslims.
rows.anchor: أي لا في نفس الأمر حال كونهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud said Quraysh looked so few at Badr that he and a companion estimated seventy and one hundred, while a captured man said they numbered one thousand.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه انه قال

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says their apparent smallness was a permanent quality resulting from the deficiency of their selves and the obscuring of their innate disposition.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي في آل عمران

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim identifies five principles for battle; patience is their foundation and fifth element. When all five combine, a force can defeat a larger enemy, as the Companions did, and each principle reinforces the others.
rows.anchor: كما قال الإمام شمس الدين محمد بن قيم الجوزية في آخر كتاب الفروسية المحمدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions’ combined discipline brought conquests; later generations’ fragmentation and weakness diminished their success. Obedient people receive strength from the One they obey.
rows.anchor: شرقا وغربا ودانت لهم العباد سلما وحربا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Abu al-Darda’s saying that Muslims fight people through their deeds; the author treats righteous conduct as an old divine rule that supports the obedient.
rows.anchor: قول أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه الذي رواه البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this principle to a passage in the fifth book of the Torah: keeping God’s commands brings blessing and rule over many peoples rather than subjection to them.
rows.anchor: قال في أثناء السفر الخامس من التوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could bring the Day or its recompense at once, but delays it only until its preordained term; He does not fear missing it.
rows.anchor: أي اليوم أو الجزاء مع ما لنا من العظمة والقدرة التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root أجل and its rearranged forms center on a set duration; al-ajal is a thing’s duration or endpoint, including death and a debt’s due date, while appointment of a term entails delay and the feminine form can mean the afterlife.
rows.anchor: بتراكيبها الأربعة : أجل وجأل وجلأ تدور على المدة المضروبة للشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other derivatives mean setting a term, delay, and the afterlife; the verb can also mean holding something back, while stirring up trouble and earning or gathering are related extensions.
rows.anchor: والتأجيل : تحديد الأجل , ويلزمه التأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also relates the root to collecting or containing things, water pools, herds of wild cattle, neck pain, and compounds made around a palm tree, explaining these as consequences of duration, enclosure, or gathering.
rows.anchor: لأنه محيط به إحاطة الأجل بالمؤجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon, cited from al-Qamus, gives related senses for أجل and لجأ: refuge and compulsion, the frog’s resort to water, the hyena’s burrow, limping, the mountain goat’s protective horns, and wound matter associated with death.
rows.anchor: قاله في القاموس , وقال في فصل الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author organizes the root’s usages around the duration itself, its end, its extension or delay, what brings the end near, its benefit, and what follows from it.
rows.anchor: إنالمادة - مع دورانها على المدة - تارة تنظر إلى نفس المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase min ajlika means ‘for your sake’ or ‘because of you’: the addressee’s existence is the reason the act was done.
rows.anchor: حقيقة أن فعلي مبتدىء من أجلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glossary completes its account of derivatives tied to collecting, enclosure, and protection, and concludes that the term in this verse means a time or appointed moment.
rows.anchor: فقد تبين أن المراد بالأجل هنا الحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza omit the yāʾ in yaʾti, relying on the preceding kasra, as is common in the Hudhayl dialect.
rows.anchor: وحذف ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة الياء اجتزاء عنها بالكسرة كما هو فاش في لغة هذيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted yāʾ evokes the terror that silences people for two thirds of the Day; the exception suggests permission to speak in its final third, since exceptions are usually smaller than their whole.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن شدة هوله تمنع أهل الموقف الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the second tāʾ in takallamu signals that no soul can utter even a little speech without permission.
rows.anchor: ولو أقل كلام بدلالة حذف التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated reference in these verses to permission from the Lord underscores His careful nurture and sound governance.
rows.anchor: أي بإذن ربك المكرر ذكره في هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assembly is divided into the wretched, whose misery was fixed and whose worldly conduct followed it, and the happy, whose fixed felicity shaped their path.
rows.anchor: ثبتت له الشقاوة فيسر في الدنيا لأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾkhir means moving something away from its direction; ajal is a time set for an event, the lām marks cause, purpose, or wisdom unlike ila, and shaqāʾ is the strength of causes of hardship.
rows.anchor: الإذهاب عن جهة الشيء بالإبعاد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched are mentioned first because most people perish and the passage is a warning, so the sequence begins with the group that makes the threat most forceful.
rows.anchor: بدأ تعالى بالأشقياء ترتيبا للنشر على ترتيب اللف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched are overcome by hardship and are judged to enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: { فأما الذين شقوا } أي أدركهم العسر والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qamus glosses zafir as exhaling after drawing breath in, and shaheeq as sobbing that reverberates in the chest.
rows.anchor: في صدره - قاله في القاموس

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir explains zafir as the exit of their breaths and shaheeq as their breaths entering.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير في تفسير سورة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says zafir is a loud sound; the segment breaks off before completing his gloss of shaheeq.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
